hypotheses.statement: Let $n\ge3$, $2\le k<n$, let $d$ be a rational metric on $X=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $s\in X^k$ be an initial labeled tuple, with repetitions allowed.

From a distinct initial tuple, any online policy has a strongly lazy online follower whose total cost on every finite word is at most the policy’s cost, for every realization of the policy’s randomness.

For every positive integer $H$, a terminating deterministic procedure on rational input constructs a rational number $a$ and a finite table defining a strongly lazy policy $\mathcal T_H$ from $u$ such that $$\label{eq:finite-table-bound}
 0\le a\le C_0\bigl(\log(k+1)\bigr)^2,\qquad
 \mathbb E\bigl[\operatorname{cost}_{\mathcal T_H,u}(w)\bigr]
 \le a\operatorname{OPT}_u(w)+D
 \quad (|w|\le H).$$ Every table decision uses exactly $b$ independent unbiased bits, where $b$ is the least nonnegative integer with $2^b\ge kH^2$.
After any raw prefix, the list represents exactly the endpoint tuples and move counts of all strongly lazy services from $u$ of the kept word using at most $M$ positive moves.
The marking rules are always feasible.

For every fixed finite sequence $\sigma$, the routine starting at any deterministic index, from arbitrary actual positions, has expected suffix cost at most $$\label{eq:suffix-bound} (4a+2)\operatorname{OPT}_s(\sigma)+(2a+2)kD.$$ Its table horizon and all parameters in Equations [eq:epoch-length]–[eq:suffix-parameters] are fixed by the instance.

Given the explicitly written constructor output of length $S$, the suffix routine can be implemented with a uniform polynomial number of bits of storage and a uniform polynomial number of bit operations per request in $L+S+2$.

There is one polynomial $p$, independent of the instance, such that preprocessing uses at most $p(L)$ bit operations and serving request $t$ uses at most $$p\bigl(L+\lceil\log_2(t+1)\rceil\bigr)$$ bit operations, for every reachable history and internal state.

outputs.exact_statement: From a distinct initial tuple, any online policy has a strongly lazy online follower whose total cost on every finite word is at most the policy’s cost, for every realization of the policy’s randomness.

For every positive integer $H$, a terminating deterministic procedure on rational input constructs a rational number $a$ and a finite table defining a strongly lazy policy $\mathcal T_H$ from $u$ such that $$\label{eq:finite-table-bound} 0\le a\le C_0\bigl(\log(k+1)\bigr)^2,\qquad \mathbb E\bigl[\operatorname{cost}_{\mathcal T_H,u}(w)\bigr] \le a\operatorname{OPT}_u(w)+D \quad (|w|\le H).$$ Every table decision uses exactly $b$ independent unbiased bits, where $b$ is the least nonnegative integer with $2^b\ge kH^2$. The procedure requires neither the value of $C_0$ nor an oracle for the policy in Theorem 2.

After any raw prefix, the list represents exactly the endpoint tuples and move counts of all strongly lazy services from $u$ of the kept word using at most $M$ positive moves. Over the entire epoch the filter creates at most $H$ entries, counting removed entries. In particular, its live list and its kept word both have size at most $H$, regardless of the number of raw requests.
The marking rules are always feasible. Following any switch, their total virtual cost over the rest of the epoch is at most $F$, including when the input ends inside a raw block.

For every fixed finite sequence $\sigma$, the routine starting at any deterministic index, from arbitrary actual positions, has expected suffix cost at most $$\label{eq:suffix-bound} (4a+2)\operatorname{OPT}_s(\sigma)+(2a+2)kD.$$ Its table horizon and all parameters in Equations [eq:epoch-length]–[eq:suffix-parameters] are fixed by the instance.

Given the explicitly written constructor output of length $S$, the suffix routine can be implemented with a uniform polynomial number of bits of storage and a uniform polynomial number of bit operations per request in $L+S+2$. These bounds hold for every reachable state and every outcome of its random choices. Each table sample uses exactly $b$ fresh unbiased random bits.

There is one polynomial $p$, independent of the instance, such that preprocessing uses at most $p(L)$ bit operations and serving request $t$ uses at most $$p\bigl(L+\lceil\log_2(t+1)\rceil\bigr)$$ bit operations, for every reachable history and internal state. Activation occurs at a finite deterministic time $t_*$ depending only on $(n,k,d)$.

purpose: Uniform computation of the squared-logarithmic k-server bound

coverage.checked_domain: All words of length at most 4 on n=3,k=2 and at most 3 on n=4,k=3, with M=0,1,2; targeted words through length 8 and M=3; uniform-metric source caps M=6 for k=2 and M=12 for k=3, plus a cap-exhausting word of length 14 at M=6.
coverage.oracle_basis: Independent exhaustive label-assignment enumeration reconstructs capped strongly lazy services from each raw prefix and separately from the kept prefix; integer checks compare multisets, created-node counts and the geometric tree bound.

title: Uniform computation of the squared-logarithmic k-server bound
